titleStmt.title: Imperial decree, published in the Pekin Gazette June 17, 1900.

head.hi: Imperial decree, published in the Pekin Gazette June 17, 1900.

div.p: Lately the people and the Christians have sought means to stir up enmity, and bad language has arisen on every side. Vagabonds have taken occasion repeatedly to burn and rob. All foreign ministers ought to be really protected. Jung Lu is ordered to detail his soldiers at once and energetically use his authority and go immediately to East Legation Street and vicinity and with all his power protect those ministers. He must not be in the least careless. If the ministers and their families wish to go for a time to Tientsin, they must be protected by the way; but the railroad is not now in working order. If they go by the cart road, it will be difficult, and there is fear that perfect protection can not be afforded. They would better, therefore, abide in peace as hitherto, and wait till the railroad is repaired and then act as circumstances render expedient.
